briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Anthropic Claude 4 push multi-agent frontiers amid rising compute race

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race accelerates with frontier labs releasing advanced reasoning models. Global compute buildout continues at pace while regulatory scrutiny intensifies on safety. Multi-agent systems emerge as the dominant paradigm for 2026 deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with 2.1T parameters focused on agentic workflows. Anthropic launched Claude 4 Opus showing gains in long-horizon planning. DeepSeek-R2 and Meta's Llama 4 compete on open weights, while xAI's Grok-3 enters enterprise testing.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New EU AI Act enforcement begins targeting high-risk agents. Red-teaming reports highlight persistent jailbreak vectors in multimodal models.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA ships Blackwell Ultra clusters to Microsoft and Google. TSMC announces 2nm AI chip production ramp. New hyperscale data centers in Texas and UAE add 50GW of dedicated AI power capacity.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will open-weight models close the capability gap with closed labs before 2027 or will proprietary scaffolding maintain the lead?
